analysis: All three changed files are test-only. LaunchAgentRestartTests.swift changes line 3 from `import MLXLMCommon` to `@testable import MLXLMCommon`, which only gives the test target access to internal symbols and has no production effect. LoadedModelsStoreTests.swift (line 104) and ProviderModelSwitchTests.swift (line 699) update the stub `LanguageModel.prepare` signature from `windowSize: Int?` to `state: LMOutput.State?, prefill: PrefillParameters`. This tracks an upstream MLXLMCommon protocol change. The stubs return `.tokens(input.text)` and hold no keys or prompt data, and no production source is modified. Nothing in the diff touches the prefix-cache storage (T-041), attestation, authorization, the coordinator WebSocket, or key handling. The environment-passthrough tests in LaunchAgentRestartTests.swift are unchanged context, and they still assert allowlisted forwarding with unrelated secrets excluded. The remaining question is whether the upstream `prepare(state:prefill:)` signature change in MLXLMCommon, together with any production call-site changes in other batches, alters prefill or KV-cache behavior relevant to T-041 and T-028. That is outside the supplied evidence, but nothing in these test changes indicates a regression.
